newsitem.title: USA: Phillips Petroleum to sell pipeline in Oklahoma.
newsitem.headline: Phillips Petroleum to sell pipeline in Oklahoma.

text.p: Phillips Petroleum Co has agreed to divest about 160 miles of its natural gas pipeline system in Oklahoma as part of a settlement with the Federal Trade Commission, the FTC said Monday.

The settlement would resolve FTC charges that Phillip's acquisition of gas-gathering assets from ANR Pipeline Co, owned by the Coastal Corp, would substantially reduce competition for natural gas gathering services in areas of five Oklahoma counties.
The affected counties are Harper, Beaver, Woods, Ellis and Woodward, the FTC said.

Phillips and ANR are two of very few companies that provide gas gathering services in each of these areas and, without the divestitures, rates would go up and drilling and production would drop, the FTC said.
In the deal at issue, Phillips, through its subsidiary GPM Gas Corp, plans to acquire ANR's gas gathering lines in the Anadarko Basin in northwest Oklahoma.
ANR transports natural gas on two mainlines, one from Louisiana and the Gulf of Mexico into Michigan, and the other from the Anadarko Basin to the upper Midwest, mainly Wisconsin.
This is the second Phillips acquisition involving gas gathering in the Anadarko Basin that the FTC has reviewed in the last 18 months.

Under the proposed consent agreement to settle the charge in this case, Phillips would be allowed to acquire the ANR assets, but would have to divest seven parts of the pipeline systems belong to ANR and Phillips in the Anadarko Basin area, in an arrangement approved by the FTC to maintain competition.
The deadline for divestiture is April 30, 1997, or within 30 days after the deal is consummated, whichever is later.

If the deadline was not met, the agreement would allow the FTC to appoint a trustee who would be authorized to include additional connecting pipeline segments in the divestiture package if that is necessary to meet a buyer's needs.

The FTC said Phillips also signed an asset maintenance agreement that requires it to keep the assets to be divested in their current condition and to provide gathering services at existing terms and conditions to customers under contract with ANR, until the divestiture.

The consent agreement also would require Phillips for 10 years to notify the FTC before acquiring during any 18-month period more than five miles of gas gathering pipelines in specified areas of the Oklahoma counties.
The commission's vote to announce the proposed consent agreement for public comment was 5-0, the FTC said.
